translation_en: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us, from Nafi' ibn 'Umar, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, from Ibn 'Abbas, that the Messenger of Allah ruled that the oath must be taken from the defendant.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us; they said: Zayd, Ibn Hubab, narrated to us: Sayf ibn Sulayman narrated to me: Qays ibn Sa'd informed me, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from Ibn 'Abbas, that the Messenger of Allah ruled on the basis of an oath and one witness.

Yahya ibn Yahya al-Tamimi narrated to us: Abu Mu'awiyah informed us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from Zaynab daughter of Abu Salamah, from Umm Salamah, who said: The Messenger of Allah said: You bring your disputes to me, and perhaps one of you is more persuasive in presenting his case than another, so I judge for him according to what I hear. If I award someone something that belongs to his brother, let him not take it, for I am only allotting him a portion of the Fire.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated this to us: Waki' narrated to us. Another chain: Abu Kurayb narrated to us: Ibn Numayr narrated to us. Both reported from Hisham with this chain, with the like of it.

Harmalah ibn Yahya narrated to me: 'Abdullah ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, who said: 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr informed me, from Zaynab daughter of Abu Salamah, from Umm Salamah, the Prophet's wife: The Messenger of Allah heard two disputants arguing at the door of her room and came out to them. He said: I am only a human being. Disputants come to me, and one may be more eloquent than another, so I may think he is truthful and rule in his favor. If I rule in someone's favor concerning a Muslim's right, it is only a piece of the Fire; let him take it or leave it.

'Amr al-Naqid narrated to us: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim ibn Sa'd narrated to us: my father narrated to us, from Salih. Another chain: 'Abd ibn Humayd informed us: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ma'mar informed us. Both reported from al-Zuhri with this chain, like Yunus's report. Ma'mar's report says that the Prophet heard a dispute at the door of Umm Salamah's room.

'Ali ibn Hujr al-Sa'di narrated to me: 'Ali ibn Mushir narrated to us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'A'ishah, who said: Hind daughter of 'Utbah, Abu Sufyan's wife, came to the Messenger of Allah and said: Messenger of Allah, Abu Sufyan is a stingy man and does not give me enough maintenance for myself and my children, except what I take from his property without his knowledge. Is there any sin on me for that? The Messenger of Allah said: Take from his property what is reasonable and enough for you and your children.

Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Numayr and Abu Kurayb narrated this to us, both from 'Abdullah ibn Numayr and Waki'. Another chain: Yahya ibn Yahya informed us: 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Muhammad narrated to us. Another chain: Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to us: Ibn Abi Fudayk narrated to us: al-Dahhak, Ibn 'Uthman, informed us. All reported from Hisham with this chain.

'Abd ibn Humayd informed us: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from 'Urwah, from 'A'ishah, who said: Hind came to the Prophet and said: Messenger of Allah, no household on earth was dearer to me to see humiliated than yours, and no household is dearer to me to see honored than yours. The Prophet said: And likewise, by the One in whose hand is my soul. Then she said: Messenger of Allah, Abu Sufyan is a miser. Is it wrong for me to spend from his wealth on his dependents without his permission? The Prophet said: There is no harm if you spend on them reasonably.

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: my nephew, al-Zuhri, narrated to us, from his uncle: 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr informed me that 'A'ishah said: Hind daughter of 'Utbah ibn Rabi'ah came and said: Messenger of Allah, no household on earth was dearer to me to see humiliated than yours, and no household today is dearer to me to see honored than yours. The Messenger of Allah said: And likewise, by the One in whose hand is my soul. Then she said: Abu Sufyan is a miser. Is there any harm if I feed our dependents from what belongs to him? He said: No, as long as it is reasonable.

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Jarir narrated to us, from Suhayl, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah said: Allah approves three things for you and dislikes three things for you. He approves that you worship Him and associate nothing with Him, that you all hold fast to Allah's rope and do not divide, and dislikes gossip, excessive questioning, and wasting wealth.

Shayban ibn Farrukh informed us: Abu 'Awanah informed us, from Suhayl, with this chain, with the like of it, except that he said Allah is displeased with three things for you, and he did not mention do not divide.

Yahya ibn Yahya al-Tamimi informed us: 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Muhammad informed us, from Yazid ibn 'Abdullah ibn Usamah ibn al-Had, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, from Busr ibn Sa'id, from Abu Qays, the freedman of 'Amr ibn al-'As, from 'Amr ibn al-'As, who heard the Messenger of Allah say: When a judge makes a judgment and strives to reach the right answer and gets it right, he has two rewards. If he makes a judgment, strives, and is mistaken, he has one reward.

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim and Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to me, both from 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Muhammad, with this chain and the like of it. At the end of the hadith, Yazid added: I related this hadith to Abu Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn Hazm, who said: Abu Salamah narrated it to me in this way, from Abu Hurayrah.

'Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Darimi narrated to me: Marwan, meaning Ibn Muhammad al-Dimashqi, informed us: al-Layth ibn Sa'd narrated to us: Yazid ibn 'Abdullah ibn Usamah ibn al-Had al-Laythi narrated to me this hadith, like the report of 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Muhammad through both chains.

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Abu 'Awanah narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umayr, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakrah, who said: My father wrote—and I wrote it for him—to 'Ubaydullah ibn Abi Bakrah, who was a judge in Sijistan: Do not judge between two people while you are angry, for I heard the Messenger of Allah say: No one should judge between two people while angry.

Yahya ibn Yahya informed us: Hushaym narrated to us. Another chain: Shayban ibn Farrukh narrated to us: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us. Another chain: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan. Another chain: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us. Another chain: 'Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh narrated to us: my father narrated to us. Both reported from Shu'bah. Another chain: Abu Kurayb narrated to us: Husayn ibn 'Ali narrated to us, from Za'idah. All of them reported from 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umayr, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakrah, from his father, from the Prophet, with the like of Abu 'Awanah's hadith.

Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah and 'Abdullah ibn 'Awn al-Hilali both narrated from Ibrahim ibn Sa'd. Ibn al-Sabbah said: Ibrahim ibn Sa'd ibn Ibrahim ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf narrated to us: my father narrated to us, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from 'A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah said: Whoever introduces into this affair of ours something that does not belong to it, it is rejected.

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim and 'Abd ibn Humayd both narrated from Abu 'Amir. 'Abd said: 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Amr narrated to us: 'Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Zuhri narrated to us, from Sa'd ibn Ibrahim, who said: I asked al-Qasim ibn Muhammad about a man who had three homes and bequeathed one third of each home. He said: Combine all of that in one home. Then he said: 'A'ishah informed me that the Messenger of Allah said: Whoever does an act that is not in accordance with our affair, it is rejected.

Yahya ibn Yahya said: I read to Malik, from 'Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr, from his father, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn 'Uthman, from Ibn Abi 'Amrah al-Ansari, from Zayd ibn Khalid al-Juhani, that the Prophet said: Shall I tell you who the best witnesses are? The one who gives his testimony before being asked for it.

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Shababah narrated to me: Warqa' narrated to me, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, who said: While two women, each with her son, were together, a wolf came and took one woman's son. One said to the other, It took your son. The other said, It took your son. They brought their case to David, who ruled the child belonged to the older woman. They then went to Solomon son of David, peace be upon them, and told him. He said, Bring me a knife so I can divide him between you. The younger woman said, May Allah have mercy on you; he is her son. Solomon ruled that the child belonged to the younger woman. Abu Hurayrah said: By Allah, I had never heard the word knife before that day; we used to say blade.

Suwayd ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Hafs, Ibn Maysarah al-San'ani, narrated to me, from Musa ibn 'Uqbah. Another chain: Umayyah ibn Bislam narrated to us: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us: Rawh, Ibn al-Qasim, narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn 'Ajlan. All of them reported from Abu al-Zinad with this chain, with the meaning of Warqa's hadith.

Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to us: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Ma'mar narrated to us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: This is what Abu Hurayrah narrated to us from the Messenger of Allah. Among those reports he said: A man bought a piece of land from another man and found a jar of gold in it. The buyer said to the seller, Take your gold; I bought the land from you and did not buy the gold. The seller said, I sold you the land and everything in it. They took their dispute to a man, who asked whether either had children. One said, I have a boy, and the other said, I have a girl. He said: Marry the boy to the girl, spend some of it on yourselves, and give charity.

Yahya ibn Yahya said: I read to Malik, from Rabi'ah ibn Abi 'Abd al-Rahman, from Yazid, the freedman of al-Munba'ith, from Zayd ibn Khalid al-Juhani, who said: A man came to the Prophet and asked about lost property. He said: Learn the description of its container and its tie, then announce it for a year. If its owner comes, return it; otherwise, you may use it. He asked about a lost sheep. The Prophet said: It is yours, your brother's, or the wolf's. He asked about a lost camel. The Prophet said: What have you to do with it? It has its water-skin and shoes; it reaches water and eats trees until its owner finds it. Yahya said: I think I read its container's description.

Yahya ibn Ayyub, Qutaybah, and Ibn Hujr narrated to us. Ibn Hujr said: Isma'il, Ibn Ja'far, informed us; the other two said: Isma'il narrated to us, from Rabi'ah ibn Abi 'Abd al-Rahman, from Yazid, the freedman of al-Munba'ith, from Zayd ibn Khalid al-Juhani: A man asked the Messenger of Allah about found property. He said: Announce it for a year, then learn its tie and container; then use it. If its owner comes, give it to him. The man asked about a lost sheep. He said: Take it; it is yours, your brother's, or the wolf's. He asked about a lost camel. The Messenger of Allah became angry until his cheeks—or his face—reddened, then said: What have you to do with it? It has its shoes and water-skin until its owner finds it.

Abu al-Tahir narrated to me: 'Abdullah ibn Wahb informed us: Sufyan al-Thawri, Malik ibn Anas, 'Amr ibn al-Harith, and others informed me that Rabi'ah ibn Abi 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to them through this chain, with the like of Malik's report. He added: A man came to the Messenger of Allah while I was with him and asked about found property. 'Amr's report says: If no one comes to claim it, use it.

Ahmad ibn 'Uthman ibn Hakim al-Awdi narrated to me: Khalid ibn Makhlad narrated to us: Sulayman, Ibn Bilal, narrated to me, from Rabi'ah ibn Abi 'Abd al-Rahman, from Yazid, the freedman of al-Munba'ith, who said: I heard Zayd ibn Khalid al-Juhani say: A man came to the Messenger of Allah. He related something like Isma'il ibn Ja'far's hadith, except he said the Prophet's face and forehead reddened and he became angry. After the words announce it for a year, he added: If its owner does not come, it remains a trust in your keeping.

'Abdullah ibn Maslamah ibn Qa'nab narrated to us: Sulayman, Ibn Bilal, narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from Yazid, the freedman of al-Munba'ith, who heard Zayd ibn Khalid al-Juhani, companion of the Messenger of Allah, say: The Messenger of Allah was asked about lost gold or silver. He said: Learn its tie and container, then announce it for a year. If you cannot identify its owner, spend it and keep it as a trust with you. If its claimant comes at any time, give it to him. He was asked about a lost camel and said: What have you to do with it? Leave it; it has its shoes and water-skin, goes to water and eats trees until its owner finds it. He was asked about a sheep and said: Take it; it is yours, your brother's, or the wolf's.

Ishaq ibn Mansur informed us: Haban ibn Hilal narrated to us: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us: Yahya ibn Sa'id and Rabi'ah ibn Abi 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to me, from Yazid, the freedman of al-Munba'ith, from Zayd ibn Khalid al-Juhani: A man asked the Prophet about a lost camel. Rabi'ah added that the Prophet became angry until his cheeks reddened. He related the hadith in a similar way and added: If its owner comes and identifies its container, quantity, and tie, give it to him; otherwise, it is yours.

Abu al-Tahir Ahmad ibn 'Amr ibn Sarh informed me: 'Abdullah ibn Wahb narrated to us: al-Dahhak ibn 'Uthman narrated to me, from Abu al-Nadr, from Busr ibn Sa'id, from Zayd ibn Khalid al-Juhani, who said: The Messenger of Allah was asked about found property. He said: Announce it for a year. If it is not claimed, learn its container and tie, then use it. If its owner comes, give it to him. Ishaq ibn Mansur narrated this to me: Abu Bakr al-Hanafi informed us: al-Dahhak ibn 'Uthman narrated to us with this chain, and in his report he said: If it is claimed, give it back; otherwise, learn its container, tie, and quantity.
